title: GitCommitResult
description: Result of the git.commit JSON-RPC method (git commit -F - — the message rides stdin, never argv, design D8). state is the outcome: zero → ok with the new head; non-zero → failed carrying git's own stdout and stderr as far as the bound allowed. We do not classify why (D11): git exposes no machine-readable discriminator between a hook, a signing failure and an index lock, and parsing prose would be a second git-error classifier. A commit that happened but whose head/status reads failed still says ok — the panel must say 'committed', not 'failed' — with the head absent and statusStale naming the gap rather than letting a fabricated zero status render as a fresh one.

head.description: Short hash of the new head; present when the post-commit head read succeeded (a failed read leaves the outcome ok with head absent — 'committed' with the head unknown).

output.description: git's own account of a failed commit (stdout and stderr as far as the bound allowed). Present when failed. The commit surface shows it and the typed message stays in the form (D11).

outputTruncated.description: True when the capture bound was reached — a silently clipped account is a worse lie than one that admits it.

status.description: The fresh post-commit status (D12). Absent when the commit failed and when the post-commit status read failed — the two cases where there is no fresh status to show.

statusStale.description: True when the commit happened but the post-commit status read failed: the panel must say the view is stale rather than render the last known lists as fresh.
